original_question: Does Baire space have a degree of categoricity in the sense of computable Polish spaces?
target_in_paper: Section 8 (Keng Meng Selwyn Ng), Problem 28: "Does the Baire space have a degree of categoricity?" The governing definition of α-categorical and degree of (topological) categoricity for computable Polish spaces is given immediately before Problems 27–29 on the same page. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact object in the paper (the Baire space) and the exact property being asked about (having a degree of categoricity in the computable-Polish-space/topological sense). So it is already very close to the official formulation of Problem 28. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
missing_details: The paper is using topological categoricity for computable Polish spaces, not ordinary computable-structure categoricity; the relevant maps are computable homeomorphisms, not isomorphisms. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
To make the question stand-alone, the Baire space should be identified explicitly as ω^ω with its usual product topology. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The quantifiers range over every pair of computable metric spaces M and N whose metric completions are homeomorphic to the given computable Polish space X. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
The degree in question is a Turing degree α. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

“Has a degree of categoricity” means that there exists a least Turing degree α such that every such pair of computable presentations admits an α-computable homeomorphism between their completions; this leastness clause is implicit in your draft and should be stated explicitly in a stand-alone version. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

No extra assumptions such as compactness, left-c.e./right-c.e. presentations, or c.e.-degree restrictions belong in this question; those appear in neighboring Problems 26 and 29, not in Problem 28. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
refined_question: Let X = ω^ω be the Baire space with its usual product topology, viewed as a computable Polish space. Does there exist a least Turing degree α such that for every pair of computable metric spaces M and N whose metric completions are homeomorphic to X, there is an α-computable homeomorphism between those completions? Equivalently stated in the paper’s terminology: does the Baire space have a degree of (topological) categoricity?
justification: This is the exact target of the draft because Section 8 first defines what it means for a computable Polish space X to be α-categorical and to have a degree of (topological) categoricity, and then immediately asks Problem 28: whether the Baire space has such a degree. The refined question simply unpacks that definition so the problem is self-contained, while staying narrower than the adjacent but different Problems 27 and 29. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
